questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My interest in the native tongue and the location in the southern Germany, which in many ways is quite different from the northern parts.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I needed some basic information about studying in Heidelberg. For instance that you can extend your semester by taking exams and writing seminar papers and that you in this way don't have to rush 30 ECTS in three months. But I didn't know that I needed that information, and no one told me.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was effortless since I just signed up through the institution and received it there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nothing much - it's generally fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up online on a website or by sending emails to the professors/ lecturers. But since there are so many courses, you can never know if a course will be cancelled for not meeting the minimum requirements of five students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know. I just contacted the professors, and they were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. No problems there.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get your hopes up until the second week begins - because of possible cancellations. Don't register for classes worth 30 ECTS, but take an exam or write a Seminararbeit/ seminar paper, which will yield something like 6 ECTS on top of the ECTS for attending the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Nothing to elaborate. The level was appropriate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style differs in that you typically attend some seminars with 5-15 people. Instead of just hearing a lecture you will be expected to participate actively, and this gives you a chance to learn a lot more than usual.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Hebräisch II: Das Buch Ruth
Hebräische Lektüre eksamensrelevanter Texte

You can learn a lot of Hebrew from Mr. Schwiderski!


Überblicksvorlesung: Einführung in das Neue Testament
Mr. Becker also has a PhD in classical philology, and therefore gives a thorough introduction into the ancient world.

Kirchengeschichte in Heidelberg
A very good way to get to know the city!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The apartment was practically empty when I moved in (except from a bed, a closet, office chair, a book shelf and a desk), so I for instance had to buy everything that I needed for the kitchen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Everything was generally - as expected - a bit cheaper in Heidelberg. 
Although getting stuff like pillows and duvets in the centre of the city is not recommended, since it's very expensive to go to Galeria as an example. Instead I would suggest going 7 kilometers south of the city centre to Jysk.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots! Climbing/ bouldering, rowing in the Neckar river, volleyball and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the bouldering group! Every wednesday evening the last semester. It's fun to climb and an easy way to meet and talk to new people - especially locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a hike to Heiligenberg (Thingstätte, Stephanus monastery, Waldschenke), get a good bike and go on a bike trip in the sorrounding area, and get a Deutschland Ticket and take the train to all of the interesting neighbouring cities: Baden-Baden, Stuttgart, Colmar, Strasbourg, Freiburg, Konstanz, Basel, and even Paris are just a short trip away.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The culture doesn't differ much from danish culture, and the people are in my experience very welcoming and nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None whatsoever.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The tendency that atleast some people tend to have more often in Germany and in smaller cities especially: Being heart warmingly polite and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Don't register for courses exclusively! Take and exam and write a seminar paper. That way you won't have a super stressed and short semester. 
2: Sign up for the sports stuff that the university offers. 
3: Concentrate on meeting locals and people with a different culture than that of your own. You can always go home after and meet new friends in your own city, but you only get so many chances to enrich your own life with other cultures - and THIS chance is a really fun one!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a bike from Radhof Bergheim. You can get some decent ones, and at the end of the semester they'll buy it right back if you kept the receipt - and for a good price if you've kept it's condition.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just the experience of living in different country. Everyday is a small adventure that you can go on according to your own wishes. It's worth all the bureaucracy!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to take 30 ECTS credits worth of classes. My schedule was completely overbooked, and since the faculty members from University of Copenhagen chose to ignore all of my emails, I didn't have the opportunity to make a change in my study programme until it was far too late.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
